_meta.indication: HARVONI is indicated for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C (CHC) genotype 1 infection in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, open-label trial that evaluated 12 and 24 weeks of HARVONI with or without ribavirin (1:1:1:1), stratified by cirrhosis and HCV genotype (1a vs 1b).
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naïve adults with genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C, with and without cirrhosis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving SVR12, with the primary hypothesis that each treatment arm was superior to a historical control rate of 60%.
pivotal_trials.n: 865 treated subjects; interim primary SVR12 analysis in the 12-week treatment groups (N=431); HARVONI 12-week arm N=214.
pivotal_trials.result: In the HARVONI 12-week arm (N=214), SVR was 99% (210/213); relapse <1% (1/212); no on-treatment virologic failures (0/213).

nct_ctgov.title: Safety and Efficacy of Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir Fixed-Dose Combination (FDC) With and Without Ribavirin for the Treatment of HCV

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label trial evaluating 12 and 24 weeks of HARVONI with or without ribavirin (1:1:1:1), stratified by cirrhosis, HCV genotype (1a vs 1b), and response to prior HCV therapy.
pivotal_trials.population: Previously-treated genotype 1 CHC adults with or without cirrhosis who failed prior therapy with an interferon-based regimen, including HCV protease inhibitor-containing regimens.
pivotal_trials.n: 440 treated subjects; HARVONI 12-week arm N=109 and 24-week arm N=109.
pivotal_trials.result: SVR was 94% (102/109) after 12 weeks and 99% (108/109) after 24 weeks of HARVONI.

nct_ctgov.title: Safety and Efficacy of Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir Fixed-Dose Combination ± Ribavirin in Treatment-Experienced Subjects With Genotype 1 HCV Infection

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label trial in treatment-naïve non-cirrhotic subjects, randomized 1:1:1 to HARVONI 8 weeks, HARVONI 12 weeks, or HARVONI + ribavirin 8 weeks; stratified by HCV genotype (1a vs 1b).
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naïve non-cirrhotic adults with genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving SVR12, with primary hypothesis that each arm was superior to a historical control rate of 60%.
pivotal_trials.n: HARVONI 8-week arm N=215 and 12-week arm N=216.
pivotal_trials.result: SVR was 94% (202/215) after 8 weeks and 96% (208/216) after 12 weeks; treatment difference (8 vs 12 weeks) -2.3% (97.5% CI -7.2% to 2.5%).

nct_ctgov.title: Safety and Efficacy of Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir Fixed-Dose Combination ± Ribavirin for the Treatment of HCV (ION-3)

key_safety: The most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥10%, all grades) with HARVONI for 8, 12, or 24 weeks were fatigue and headache. Fatigue occurred in 16%/13%/18% and headache in 11%/14%/17% of subjects at 8/12/24 weeks, respectively.
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination of ledipasvir, an HCV NS5A inhibitor, and sofosbuvir, a nucleotide analog inhibitor of the HCV NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase; both proteins are required for viral replication.
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination of two oral small-molecule direct-acting antivirals).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected and outside expertise was not necessary.

basis.text: Designated a Breakthrough Therapy because preliminary clinical evidence indicated substantial improvement over available therapies in treating CHC-infected adults, including the first ribavirin-free regimen for genotype 1.

citations.quote: In addition, the FDC was designated as a Breakthrough Therapy under FDASIA, Title IX because preliminary clinical evidence indicated substantial improvement over available therapies in the treatment of CHC-infected adults including the first ribavirin-free regimen for GT1.

basis.text: Granted priority review because CHC is a serious and life-threatening disease and the FDC appeared to provide improvement in safety and effectiveness.

citations.quote: The application was granted a priority review because CHC is a serious and life-threatening disease and the FDC appeared to provide improvement in safety and effectiveness.

summary.text: HARVONI received a priority review and Breakthrough Therapy designation; it was approved first cycle for chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 infection in adults based on three Phase 3 trials (ION-1, ION-2, ION-3), without accelerated approval.

citations.quote: The application was granted a priority review because CHC is a serious and life-threatening disease and the FDC appeared to provide improvement in safety and effectiveness.

In addition, the FDC was designated as a Breakthrough Therapy under FDASIA, Title IX because preliminary clinical evidence indicated substantial improvement over available therapies in the treatment of CHC-infected adults including the first ribavirin-free regimen for GT1.
The Phase 3 program encompasses treatment-naïve and treatment experienced patient populations with GT1 who enrolled in three principal clinical trials, ION-1, ION-2 and ION-3.
